ref: Standard form of quadratic equation SolvedEx.1 (1)
subtopic: Standard Form of a Quadratic Equation
context: Decide which of the following are quadratic equations ?
setLabel: Standard form of quadratic equation SolvedEx.1
solution:
In the equation \(3x^2 - 5x + 3 = 0\), \(x\) is the only variable and maximum index of the variable is 2.

\(\therefore\) It is a quadratic equation.

\(\therefore\) It is a quadratic equation.

ref: Standard form of quadratic equation SolvedEx.1 (3)
subtopic: Standard Form of a Quadratic Equation
context: Decide which of the following are quadratic equations ?
setLabel: Standard form of quadratic equation SolvedEx.1
solution:
In the equation \(m^3 - 5m^2 + 4 = 0\), \(m\) is the only variable but maximum index of the variable is not 2.

\(\therefore\) It is not a quadratic equation.

ref: Standard form of quadratic equation SolvedEx.1 (4)
subtopic: Standard Form of a Quadratic Equation
context: Decide which of the following are quadratic equations ?
setLabel: Standard form of quadratic equation SolvedEx.1
solution:
\((l + 2)(l - 5) = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(l(l - 5) + 2(l - 5) = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(l^2 - 5l + 2l - 10 = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(l^2 - 3l - 10 = 0\). In this equation \(l\) is the only variable and maximum index of the variable is 2.

\(\therefore\) It is a quadratic equation.

(The textbook prints this part of the worked solution with blank boxes for the student to fill in; the completed entries are shown above.)

ref: Roots of a quadratic equation SolvedEx.1
stem: \(2x^2 - 7x + 6 = 0\) check whether (i) \(x = \dfrac{3}{2}\), (ii) \(x = -2\) are solutions of the equations.
solution:
(i) Put \(x = \dfrac{3}{2}\) in the polynomial \(2x^2 - 7x + 6\)

\(2x^2 - 7x + 6 = 2\left(\dfrac{3}{2}\right)^2 - 7\left(\dfrac{3}{2}\right) + 6\)

\(= 2 \times \dfrac{9}{4} - \dfrac{21}{2} + 6\)

\(= \dfrac{9}{2} - \dfrac{21}{2} + \dfrac{12}{2} = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(x = \dfrac{3}{2}\) is a solution of the equation.

(ii) Let \(x = -2\) in \(2x^2 - 7x + 6\)

\(2x^2 - 7x + 6 = 2(-2)^2 - 7(-2) + 6\)

\(= 2 \times 4 + 14 + 6\)

\(= 28 \neq 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(x = -2\) is not a solution of the equation.
